bugs: Evaluation is a recursive AST walk. Deep nesting depends on temporarily raising sys.recursionlimit to 20000, which can overflow the C stack on some platforms or threads. A RecursionError during evaluation is silently turned into #VALUE! instead of a defined behaviour.
Every structural edit rebuilds all indexes and recalculates the whole sheet (about 1–1.4 s at 50k cells). This is documented, but it scales poorly and calls self.__init__() to reset state.
Whitespace around a range's ':' (A1 : B2) does not form a range token, so such formulas are #PARSE! (a minor divergence).

Relies on sys.setrecursionlimit(20000) during set/copy/structural edits: a process-global, non-reentrant side effect; parse/eval recursion is still bounded, with deep formulas silently degrading to #PARSE!/#VALUE! via caught RecursionError.
Sheet exposes extra public methods `value` and `iter_rect` (it doubles as the evaluation Context), leaking beyond the fixed API.
Negative zero is not normalised (`=-B1` with empty B1 yields -0.0; ROUND(-0.4,0) yields -0.0); cosmetic but observable via str().
RangeIndex never prunes emptied tile dicts, and 16-column tiles mean an edit in column C scans every range registered over column A in the same tile (e.g. thousands of prefix sums).

Evaluation is a recursive AST walk. Deep nesting only works because set/copy/_restructure temporarily raise sys.setrecursionlimit to 20000, which is process-global, not thread-safe and could still overflow the C stack. _evaluate also catches RecursionError and silently returns #VALUE!.
Ranges spanning more than 256 tiles go into one _untiled dict that every dependency lookup scans linearly. Many distinct large ranges therefore make each edit O(#large ranges).
Structural edits re-store every cell and recalculate the whole sheet (about 1-1.4s per edit at 50k cells, per the notes). _restructure resets state by calling self.__init__().
There is no dirty-pruning: every transitive dependent is re-evaluated even when an intermediate value did not change, and prefix-sum sheets are quadratic (acknowledged in the notes).

Recursive-descent parser and recursive AST evaluation rely on `sys.setrecursionlimit(20000)` set/restored around every set/copy/structural call; process-global mutation, and nesting beyond the limit silently degrades to #PARSE!/#VALUE! via caught RecursionError.
Structural edits rebuild the whole sheet (`self.__init__()` then re-store everything) and recalculate every cell: O(sheet) per insert/delete.

RangeIndex: any range spanning more than 256 tiles (e.g. a single-column range taller than ~16k rows) goes to an untiled list scanned on every lookup, so thousands of tall column SUMs slow down edits anywhere on the sheet; within a tile every rect is scanned too.
Negative zero is not normalised (`=-0*1` returns -0.0; ROUND(-0.4,0) gives -0.0) — cosmetic.
`_check_axis` does no type check: `insert_rows(1.5)` produces float cell keys and corrupts the store.
Off-grid references in formulas evaluate to #NAME? and a range with an off-grid endpoint is #PARSE! (documented decision, but surprising given #REF! exists).
Sheet exposes extra non-API public methods `value` and `iter_rect`.

bugs: copy() iterates every coordinate of the source block, not just populated cells, so copying a huge sparse range (for example a whole column) means millions of iterations.
API addresses accept leading-zero rows ('A01') and copy silently strips '$'. This is lenient but documented.
copy() iterates the entire dense source rectangle (e.g. copy('A1:A1048576','B1') walks ~1M positions and seeds _recalc with ~1M keys) regardless of how many cells are populated.
API addresses with leading zeros (`A01`) are accepted even though the spec says malformed addresses raise ValueError (documented decision, but inconsistent with rejecting whitespace/`$`).
delete_rows/delete_cols running past the grid edge are not validated.
Function arity lives in `_formula.ARITY` while implementations live in `_evaluator.FUNCTIONS`; the compiler special-cases IF/IFERROR/aggregates by name, so adding a function touches several places.

copy iterates every cell of the source rectangle and stores and recalcs each one, including empty cells. Copying a whole column (A1:A1048576) does about a million _store calls and creates a million-element seed list, so it is unusable for large sparse ranges.
Lenient tokenization in rewrite skips untokenizable characters one at a time. Inside an unterminated string (e.g. '="abc A1'), text after the quote can be treated as a reference and rewritten.
delete_rows/delete_cols do not reject a deletion that runs past the grid edge, unlike the other validation.
Both function arity (ARITY in _formula.py) and implementations (FUNCTIONS in _evaluator.py) must be kept in sync by hand, and IF/IFERROR are special-cased in the compiler.
`copy` and `_parse_range` call `.replace('$', '')` before validating the type, so a non-str src/dst raises AttributeError instead of ValueError.

`copy` iterates every position of the source rectangle (not just populated cells) and seeds recalc with every key, so copying a large sparse block such as a whole column does ~1M iterations, stores and index lookups.
Deleting past the grid edge (`delete_rows(1048576, 2)`) is accepted silently; the other two submissions reject it.
Lenient re-tokenisation for rewriting skips an unterminated quote and then treats the rest as tokens, so `="abc & A1` gets its `A1` rewritten although it is inside a (broken) string literal.
strengths: No recursion anywhere: a shunting-yard parser, compilation driven by an explicit stack, and a flat stack VM with jumps for IF and IFERROR.
Incremental structural edits that rewrite and recompile only affected formulas, seeded with dependents of removed cells.

SCC ordering restricted to formula cells avoids O(n²) literal edges.

Non-recursive pipeline: shunting-yard parser, compilation to flat code with jumps, and a VM. Iterative Tarjan restricted to formula cells, avoiding literal-to-formula edge blowup.

bugs: Formulas that fail to parse are never rewritten by structural edits or copy. Their reference text then silently points at different cells after rows or columns move. This is a documented decision, but it contradicts 'formulas everywhere are rewritten'.
When a rewritten range token is written out, the original whitespace around ':' is dropped. This is minor and documented.
Unparseable formulas are copied and moved with their reference tokens untouched (documented), which diverges from the brief's statement that structural edits and copies rewrite reference tokens.
DependencyIndex.dependents() returns live internal containers (a tuple or the actual set) that callers must not mutate; an easy future footgun.
ArgumentTypeError inheriting from both TypeError and ValueError is unusual and could surprise callers.
Formula.relocated() duplicates the text-rewrite semantics in code form; the two must stay in lockstep (mitigated by the differential test).

Formulas that fail to parse are never rewritten by structural edits or copy. Their reference tokens go stale after rows or columns move. This is a documented choice, but arguably contradicts the brief's rewrite rule.
ArgumentTypeError subclasses both TypeError and ValueError. This is unusual API surface beyond the spec.
Performance tests have tight wall-clock budgets (the chain test runs 2.0-2.7s against a 3s limit, per the notes), so they are likely flaky on slower CI.
No correctness bugs found. Minor: `=A1 (2)` lexes `A1` as a function name (#NAME?) rather than #PARSE!, and a ref immediately followed by whitespace+'(' is silently treated as a call.
Formulas that fail to parse are never rewritten by structural edits or copy (documented), so fixing a typo later leaves stale references — a usability trap rather than a spec violation.
Dependents() hands out live internal sets ('must not be mutated'); safe today because recalc never touches the index, but a fragile contract.
strengths: Fully iterative pipeline (lexer → shunting-yard → codegen → VM) that never touches the recursion limit.

Kahn's algorithm orders the acyclic part and Tarjan runs only on the leftover. Value-change-driven dirty propagation skips unaffected downstream cells, and there is a fast path for edits nobody reads.
A dyadic 2-D range index scales to whole-grid ranges.
Structural edits are incremental: compiled code is relocated rather than re-parsed, and only lossy references trigger recalculation.
Excellent tests, including a randomized differential test against freshly built sheets and change-list verification, plus thorough edge-case and performance tests.
Very thorough NOTES with explicit rationale for each decision.
Everything iterative, with a compact stack VM; reference operands travel unread as int tuples so single refs in aggregates behave as 1-cell ranges at runtime and compiled code is GC-cheap.
Dyadic 2-D range index gives exact O(log n) coverage per range and cheap point lookups.

Smartest recalculation: Kahn for the acyclic part, Tarjan only for leftovers, dirty-tracking so untouched downstream cells are not re-evaluated, fast path for cells nobody reads, and a lossy-only recalc after structural edits with a reach cutoff.
